title_prefix: A failed announcement is deleted rather
mechanism: Both the notfound path (tx-request-notfound, src/networking/protocol.lisp:476-486) and the 60s expiry path (retry-timed-out-tx-requests, :586-637) call %tx-request-drop-announcer (:411-425), which REMOVES the announcement and decrements the peer's *tx-peer-announcements* budget. Core's MakeCompleted (refs/bitcoin/src/txrequest.cpp:456-478) converts the announcement to State::COMPLETED instead; the COMPLETED announcement keeps the (peer, txhash) slot of the ByPeer index, so ReceivedInv's emplace fails and a re-announcement from that peer is a no-op (:578-592), and Count(peer) -- the value MAX_PEER_TX_ANNOUNCEMENTS is checked against -- includes COMPLETED announcements (:m_total, txrequest.cpp Count). ONE CORRECTION to the finder: the headline probe (1000 grants to a single peer over 1000 announce/notfound rounds) is NOT a divergence. When the failing peer is the only announcer, Core's IsOnlyNonCompleted holds and MakeCompleted ERASES every announcement for that txhash (txrequest.cpp:463-470), a rule txrequest.h:52 states explicitly ('If for a given txhash only already-failed announcements remain, they are all forgotten'), so Core's re-inv from that peer is also a fresh candidate and is also granted. The divergence exists only while another non-COMPLETED announcement for the same txhash is alive.
consequence: While an honest announcement keeps the entry alive, we let the failed peer re-enter the candidate set immediately and we refund its per-peer announcement budget. Two concrete effects, both executed: (a) MAX_PEER_TX_ANNOUNCEMENTS stops bounding failed requests -- over 20,000 announce/notfound rounds with a live co-announcer the attacker's Count peaked at 1 while the honest peer that never resolved reached exactly the 5,000 cap, so Core would have frozen the attacker out after 5,000 failures and we never do; (b) the attacker gets extra GETDATA_TX_INTERVAL windows on the same transaction -- in the expiry-driven sequence it held 2 of the 3 windows the transaction lived through, where Core allows it exactly one. This is the invariant txrequest.h:45-58 exists to protect ('The same transaction is never requested twice from the same peer, unless the announcement was forgotten in between ... giving a peer multiple chances to announce a transaction would allow them to bias requests in their favor, worsening transaction censoring attacks'). Two real bounds keep it off S1: an inbound (non-preferred) attacker cannot take the request from an outbound honest announcer at all, and each re-inv costs the peer's inv bucket (50/s sustained, burst 200). S2: a censorship and request-burn lever with no cap, not memory growth or a crash.
evidence: (1) ga11-p3-single-announcer, the finder's headline probe reproduced: (:ROUNDS 1000 :GRANTS 1000 :ENTRY-LEFT NIL :COUNT-AFTER 0) -- reproduced but NOT a divergence, see the mechanism note on txrequest.cpp:463-470. (2) ga11-p3-reannounce-with-live-coannouncer, the real divergence: (:FIRST-GRANT T :HONEST-GRANT NIL :DUPLICATE-INV-RECORDED NIL :COUNT-AFTER-DUPLICATE 1 :AFTER-NOTFOUND (:ATK-COUNT 0 :HON-COUNT 1 :ANNOUNCERS 1) :REANNOUNCEMENT-RECORDED (:RETURNED T :ATK-COUNT 1 :ANNOUNCERS 2)) -- a duplicate inv while the announcement lives is correctly a no-op, and the notfound is what unlocks re-entry. (3) ga11-p3-budget-peak-before-notfound, 20,000 rounds: (:PEAK-ATTACKER-COUNT 1 :CAP 5000 :HONEST-COUNT 5000) -- the honest peer reaching exactly 5,000 is the positive control that the cap is enforced and that the notfound path is what escapes it. (4) ga11-p3-expiry-windows through the shipped handlers with backdated expiry: (:CYCLES 10 :ATTACKER-WINDOWS 2 :HONEST-WINDOWS 1 :STILL-TRACKED NIL). (5) Counter-probe ga11-p3-preferred-honest-wins: (:ATTACKER-SELECTED-TIMES 0 :NOTFOUND-HAS-RATE-BUCKET NIL :INV-RATE-BUCKET (50.0 . 200.0)). Ours: src/networking/protocol.lisp:411-425, :476-486, :586-637, :338-341 (+max-peer-tx-announcements+ 5000). Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/txrequest.cpp:436-478, :484-500, :578-592, :660-670 (Count); refs/bitcoin/src/txrequest.h:45-58.
fix_shape: Give an announcement a state instead of deleting it. Carry a completed flag on each (peer . ready) entry in *tx-announcers*; tx-request-notfound and the expiry arm of retry-timed-out-tx-requests set that flag rather than calling %tx-request-drop-announcer, and %tx-request-best-candidate skips completed entries. Reproduce Core's two deletion rules exactly: when the entry being completed is the last non-completed announcement for the hash, erase them all (MakeCompleted / IsOnlyNonCompleted, txrequest.cpp:463-470), and erase everything on ForgetTxHash and on peer disconnect. tx-request-wanted-p must then treat a completed announcement from the same peer the way it already treats a live one -- return NIL and record nothing (ReceivedInv's ByPeer uniqueness, :578-592) -- and *tx-peer-announcements* must keep counting completed entries so MAX_PEER_TX_ANNOUNCEMENTS charges failures, which is Core's m_total. This same state is what finding dd85e71f's per-peer ReceivedResponse needs, so the two fixes are one change.
